title: [assembly] Enforce assembly and agent coding standards
outcome: Version and enforce one assembly, review, safety, and optimization contract for every human and coding agent.
audit: Audited frame.asm structure, existing comments, README build instructions, and every repository-level agent adapter.
acceptance: AGENTS.md is authoritative and adapter guidance is additive.
NASM policy checks reject unsafe or inconsistent constructs.
Assembly and optimization reference notes are linked from contributor guidance.

title: [assembly] Map frame.asm into auditable ownership modules
outcome: Define coherent source-region ownership and a measured extraction strategy without destabilizing the freestanding binary.
audit: Inventory global labels, tables, request dispatch, compositor, input, DRM, and cleanup regions before proposing boundaries.
acceptance: A dependency map identifies state ownership and cross-region calls.
Any extraction preserves byte-level behavior and reproducible output or documents the intentional delta.
Reviewers can trace cleanup and resource ownership without hidden generated code.

title: [performance] Review low-level optimization references and publish a measured playbook
outcome: Turn the approved assembly/programming reference corpus into a source-grounded optimization and review playbook for frame.
audit: Locate the authorized ebook/reference corpus, record editions and relevant chapters, and compare recommendations with current hot paths.
acceptance: References and licensing/access boundaries are recorded without copying protected books.
The playbook covers cache, branches, dependencies, syscalls, SIMD tradeoffs, and llvm-mca/perf use.
Every recommendation distinguishes measured evidence from hypothesis.

title: [build] Establish the layered headless test harness and manifest
outcome: Provide deterministic unit, static, integration, regression, fuzz, reproducibility, and manual acceptance lanes with explicit ownership.
audit: Audited existing ad-hoc test output, server startup flags, socket paths, and hardware-affecting modes.
acceptance: tests/manifest.json owns every suite and hardware boundary.
All automated server tests use isolated numeric displays, temporary HOME, --noinput, and cleanup assertions.
Make targets give contributors and CI one canonical interface.

title: [protocol] Expand the core request, reply, error, and event regression matrix
outcome: Give every supported core request a positive, boundary, malformed, sequence, and client-isolation test where applicable.
audit: Compare the dispatch table and implemented handlers with tests/lib/x11.py and the current regression suite.
acceptance: The opcode matrix links every implemented request to tests and canonical semantics.
Variable payload truncation cannot consume the next request.
Errors and replies carry the correct sequence and do not kill unrelated clients.

title: [security] Add deterministic malformed-input and multi-client isolation corpora
outcome: Replay bounded hostile setup/request streams and prove the server and unaffected clients remain available.
audit: Inventory setup parsing, length arithmetic, resource lookup, capacity limits, and disconnect cleanup before selecting seeds.
acceptance: Seeds cover truncation, overflow boundaries, bad IDs, unsupported byte order, and interleaved clients.
Runs have monotonic deadlines and retain useful redacted diagnostics.
The corpus is deterministic, hardware-free, and bounded for CI.

title: [build] Enforce reproducible builds and the linked ELF security contract
outcome: Prove two clean builds are byte-identical and the ELF is static, non-executable-stack, W^X, relocation-free, and within reviewed memory bounds.
audit: Audited NASM/LD flags, sections, program headers, relocation output, build IDs, and BSS footprint.
acceptance: Linker and assembler warnings are fatal.
Static ELF policy reports actionable failures.
Two isolated builds produce the same SHA-256.

title: [build] Install read-only CI and trusted self-hosted runner gates
outcome: Run untrusted pull requests only on hosted read-only jobs and reserve repo-scoped self-hosted runners for trusted main, tags, or approved dispatches.
audit: Reviewed dagobah-infra and tsctl runner patterns, GitHub permission boundaries, frame hardware modes, and required status checks.
acceptance: Actions are pinned to immutable SHAs with least-privilege permissions.
Runner safety fails closed on root, hardware devices, live displays, KVM, or container sockets.
Self-hosted workflows are opt-in and never execute fork code with secrets.

title: [security] Enforce secrets, dependency, source, and binary scanning
outcome: Prevent credentials and high-confidence security defects from entering history or release artifacts.
audit: Audited git history, working tree, staged hooks, AWS credential patterns, dependency sources, ELF hardening, and GitHub security settings.
acceptance: git-secrets and Gitleaks cover staged content, tree, and reachable history without echoing suspected values.
GitHub secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot, dependency review, and private reporting are enabled.
Extended source/binary/image scans run only in trusted lanes with redacted artifacts.

title: [build] Integrate SonarQube assembly policy and quality gating
outcome: Import versioned NASM policy findings into SonarQube and wait for the project quality gate on trusted source.
audit: Confirmed native Sonar language coverage limits and mapped assembly/security rules into generic external-issue JSON.
acceptance: Assembly findings have stable rule IDs, severity, locations, and remediation text.
The scanner uses an approval-protected environment and never exposes tokens to forks.
The workflow waits for and reports the Sonar quality gate.

title: [release] Deliver reproducible packages, SBOMs, OCI images, attestations, and ECR publication
outcome: Turn validated SemVer tags into immutable native and OCI artifacts with checksums, SBOMs, scans, attestations, and approval-gated ECR aliases.
audit: Reviewed tsctl and dagobah-infra delivery patterns, rootless image tooling, current ECR variables, and frame's static runtime requirements.
acceptance: Build and publish jobs are separated and use immutable version/SHA identities.
Artifacts include checksums, SPDX/CycloneDX SBOMs, vulnerability results, and provenance attestations.
ECR repository, OIDC role, lifecycle policy, and release approval exist before ECR_ENABLED is set true.
dependencies: external: ECR repository and GitHub OIDC role

title: [agents] Publish coding-agent roles, dispatch rules, and review handoffs
outcome: Give every coding agent the same issue-first, safety, testing, review, optimization, and delivery contract.
audit: Compared repository adapters with the tsctl shared bootstrap, issue taxonomy, dispatch gates, and assembly-specific requirements.
acceptance: Agent adapters reference one authoritative AGENTS.md without weakening it.
Auditor, implementer, reviewer, optimizer, and orchestrator responsibilities are explicit.
Cluster dispatch requires SDD-complete issues, safe capacity, canonical validation, and PR/branch reconciliation.

title: [protocol] Publish the core opcode conformance matrix from xorgproto and X.Org
outcome: Map every core opcode to implemented behavior, canonical semantics, reply/error expectations, tests, and compatibility status.
audit: Read the current dispatch table and handler labels, then compare each request with xorgproto and canonical X.Org dix sources.
acceptance: All 127 core opcode slots have an explicit status.
Reply-bearing gaps and framing hazards are prioritized ahead of void cosmetic gaps.
Every deliberate incompatibility cites evidence and client impact.

title: [protocol] Conform setup, authentication framing, resource IDs, replies, errors, and sequences
outcome: Make connection setup and common reply/error sequencing safe across fragmentation, malformed clients, and concurrent resource ranges.
audit: Audit setup_header handling, auth-tail draining, byte-order rejection, client bases/masks, sequence increments, and error writers.
acceptance: Fragmented and coalesced setup/auth payloads are handled without stream loss.
Each client receives a disjoint valid ID range.
Replies and errors use the triggering request sequence and preserve unrelated clients.

title: [protocol] Complete property, selection, event, and window-management requests
outcome: Finish the core request families required by ICCCM/EWMH window managers and representative desktop clients.
audit: Use the core conformance matrix and real-client traces to identify missing reply-bearing and stateful requests before implementation.
acceptance: Property formats/lengths, selection ownership/conversion, event masks/propagation, and window tree transitions match canonical semantics.
Bad IDs, values, access, allocation, and match cases return bounded errors.
Each added handler has positive, malformed, cross-client, and cleanup coverage.

title: [protocol] Decide the byte-swapped client support boundary
outcome: Choose and document either complete swapped-client support or a durable fail-closed little-endian-only contract.
audit: Inventory every setup, dispatch, variable payload, reply, event, error, and extension swap obligation; do not infer feasibility from setup alone.
acceptance: The decision records scope, security risk, test cost, client demand, and maintenance impact.
No isolated byte swaps are merged without an end-to-end design.
The advertised/documented compatibility boundary matches runtime behavior.

title: [security] Audit resource ownership and cross-client authorization
outcome: Map ownership, lookup authorization, capacity, dependencies, and cleanup for every core and extension resource table.
audit: Inventory all XID-bearing tables, owner fields, lookup helpers, allocation loops, destroy paths, extension state, and client disconnect cleanup.
acceptance: Every resource type has one lifecycle record with creation, use, cascade, and reclamation semantics.
Cross-client authorization gaps and stale-slot risks become scoped child defects.
The audit includes selections, grabs, subscriptions, SHM, redirect claims, and non-XID client state.

title: [protocol] Prove disconnect cleanup, dependency cascades, and clean slot reuse
outcome: Destroy one client at every lifecycle point and prove all owned/dependent state is reclaimed without affecting another client.
audit: Trace client_disconnect and every explicit free/destroy handler against the resource audit before adding fixtures.
acceptance: Tests cover windows/children, pixmaps, GCs, fonts, cursors, selections, grabs, subscriptions, extension resources, and partial creation.
A new client reusing slots sees zero stale state.
Cleanup remains bounded under capacity exhaustion and malformed disconnects.

title: [security] Bound tables, allocations, and client-driven denial-of-service paths
outcome: Make all client-controlled counts, dimensions, allocations, loops, and fixed tables fail closed before overflow or unbounded work.
audit: Search width/height/bpp products, count-derived lengths, mmap sizes, table scans, reply growth, event queues, and resource exhaustion branches.
acceptance: Arithmetic uses checked bounds before multiplication/addition and before syscalls.
Capacity exhaustion yields a bounded protocol error or isolated disconnect without corrupting tables.
Fuzz/regression seeds preserve server availability and bounded runtime.

title: [render] Build pixel-exact core drawing and GC conformance fixtures
outcome: Validate exact pixels and protocol semantics for supported core drawing requests, drawables, GCs, clipping, and text.
audit: Inventory core drawing handlers, GC fields, drawable lookup, bounds/clip helpers, font tables, and GetImage behavior.
acceptance: Fixtures cover foreground/background, raster ops, plane mask, origins, clips, overlap, negative coordinates, and edges.
ImageText/PolyText font metrics and transparent/image semantics match canonical behavior.
Malformed payloads preserve stream framing and drawable contents.

title: [render] Complete RENDER operators and picture-format conformance
outcome: Implement only the advertised RENDER formats, pictures, operators, transforms, clips, glyphs, and cleanup semantics required by clients.
audit: Map the RENDER dispatch/version advertisement to xorgproto, render/ source, toolkit traces, and existing picture/glyph tables.
acceptance: Advertised formats and versions match implemented requests.
Pixel fixtures cover supported alpha/composite operators and error cases.
Picture/glyph resources are owner-checked and reclaimed on free/disconnect.

title: [compositor] Prove damage, exposure, stacking, backing, and clipping semantics
outcome: Make mapped window trees repaint deterministically through move, resize, map, unmap, restack, overlap, and partial damage.
audit: Trace window records, backing allocation, map state, child traversal, damage union, exposure generation, and compositor flush paths.
acceptance: Direct-child and recursive tree behavior is explicit and tested.
Occlusion, clipping, borders, background, exposure, and stale-pixel cases have pixel evidence.
Damage never escapes framebuffer/backing bounds or leaves mapped content stale.

title: [performance] Reduce compositor repaint and text-render bandwidth after measurement
outcome: Lower active desktop CPU and private memory without changing protocol pixels, safety, or observability.
audit: Use compositor counters and matched workloads to distinguish glyph raster, damage granularity, full-window composition, flush, and allocation costs.
acceptance: A repeatable baseline identifies a specific hotspot and noise controls.
The change has pixel/regression equivalence and before/after distributions.
Results report CPU, PSS/private memory, syscalls, context switches, bytes/pixels, code size, and maintenance tradeoffs.

title: [input] Build a synthetic keyboard, pointer, grab, drag, and resize harness
outcome: Exercise interactive input routing deterministically without opening /dev/input or the user's live display.
audit: Inventory FIFO/synthetic input hooks, core/XI event writers, focus, passive/active grabs, pointer state, cursor state, and tswm interaction expectations.
acceptance: The harness scripts key, button, motion, enter/leave, focus, drag, and resize sequences.
Event ordering, coordinates, masks, time, focus, and grab routing are asserted.
Every run uses an isolated display, --noinput, a temporary HOME, deadlines, and cleanup.

title: [xkb] Implement Firefox-compatible XKB discovery, maps, state, and events
outcome: Satisfy the XKB request/event subset required by Firefox and representative toolkits for usable keyboard input and layout state.
audit: Trace Firefox/toolkit XKB startup against xkbproto, X.Org xkb/ handlers, current opcode tables, and advertised versions.
acceptance: UseExtension, SelectEvents, GetMap, GetNames, GetState, and required related requests match negotiated versions and lengths.
Representative US and one non-US layout produce expected symbols/state.
Unsupported XKB surface is not falsely advertised and malformed clients remain isolated.

title: [input] Prove focus, grabs, cursor, and multi-window interaction parity
outcome: Verify real window-manager focus and pointer workflows across multiple mapped clients without stuck grabs, cursors, or routing state.
audit: Use tswm interaction flows and server diagnostics to enumerate click-to-focus, focus cycling, modal grabs, frame controls, drag, resize, close, and disconnect cases.
acceptance: Each flow asserts semantic window state and visible geometry before/after.
Destroy/disconnect during grabs leaves no stale focus, grab, cursor, or button state.
The same scripted flow passes on the control X server and frame, with documented intentional differences.

title: [extensions] Publish the advertised extension and version compatibility matrix
outcome: Map every advertised extension/version to requests, replies, events, errors, resources, tests, and real-client demand.
audit: Inventory QueryExtension/ListExtensions tables and every extension dispatch block, then compare xorgproto and client traces.
acceptance: Every advertised extension has a version and request-by-request status.
Reply-bearing gaps, wrong lengths, and over-advertised versions are prioritized.
The matrix links canonical source, fixtures, representative clients, and deliberate omissions.

title: [extensions] Complete RandR, XFixes, Damage, Composite, and SHM startup contracts
outcome: Provide the coherent extension subsets required by tswm, terminals, Firefox, and representative toolkits without reply deadlocks.
audit: Use the extension matrix and captured startup traces to define exact version/request/resource scope before implementation.
acceptance: Negotiated versions do not exceed implemented behavior.
Every reply/event/error wire layout has protocol fixtures and malformed coverage.
Extension subscriptions/resources are bounded, owner-checked, and cleaned up.

title: [extensions] Complete XInput2 requests, events, hierarchy, and device cleanup
outcome: Expose a consistent master pointer/keyboard hierarchy and the XI2 subset demanded by modern toolkits.
audit: Compare current XIQueryVersion/XIQueryDevice/event encoding with xinputproto, X.Org Xi/, toolkit traces, and synthetic input routing.
acceptance: Version negotiation, device classes, masks, event lengths, coordinates, focus, and hierarchy are internally consistent.
Unknown devices, masks, and lengths fail safely.
Subscriptions and per-client XI state are reclaimed on disconnect.

title: [drm] Harden DRM acquisition, modeset, signal cleanup, and CRTC restore
outcome: Make every DRM acquisition stage reversible on syscall failure, signal, normal exit, or partial initialization.
audit: Trace card discovery, master acquisition, connector/encoder/CRTC selection, dumb buffers, FB IDs, mmap, cursor, page flip, and restore order.
acceptance: Each live resource has explicit state and one reverse-order cleanup path.
Fault-injection/static tests cover every pre-hardware failure edge.
Manual TTY evidence proves original CRTC and subsequent display-server health.

title: [drm] Validate page flip, VT switch, multi-output, hotplug, and device loss
outcome: Record recovery-safe hardware behavior across display topology and ownership transitions.
audit: Map poll descriptors, flip state, output tables, VT release/acquire, hotplug rebuild, timeout, and error/hangup branches before manual execution.
acceptance: Single/dual output, flip completion/failure, VT away/back, connect/disconnect, and DRM loss are recorded.
No busy loop, stale scanout, stuck master, or leaked framebuffer remains.
The original desktop/console recovers after every case.

title: [input] Validate evdev enumeration, unplug, permissions, and cleanup
outcome: Prove live input devices are opened, parsed, removed, and released safely under a documented least-privilege policy.
audit: Trace device enumeration, capability checks, partial/batched input_event reads, poll rebuild, unplug, permission denial, and shutdown.
acceptance: Permission denial degrades safely without recommending blanket root execution.
Partial records, batched records, and unplug cannot leave stale poll entries or grabs.
Synthetic and live routing produce equivalent X events for the accepted matrix.

title: [drm] Execute the recorded bare-console hardware acceptance matrix
outcome: Complete a human-controlled release-candidate TTY run with hardware, recovery, and post-test health evidence.
audit: Review all E09 implementation evidence and tests/manual/README.md before selecting the exact host, GPU, connector, input, and recovery path.
acceptance: The record includes commit, host, CPU/GPU/driver/kernel, permissions, commands, logs, expected/actual, cleanup, and recovery.
No other graphical session owns DRM during the run.
The prior display manager and all devices are healthy afterward.

title: [protocol] Reach tswm/xterm visual parity and profile server cost
outcome: Run tswm and a visibly usable xterm prompt directly on frame, with protocol gaps and server/session costs recorded.
audit: Compared real tswm/xterm traces with X.Org QueryColors, ImageText8, PolyText8, and MapSubwindows semantics and inspected resulting framebuffer pixels.
acceptance: tswm bar, decorations, xterm text, prompt, and cursor are visible and stable.
QueryColors, ImageText8, PolyText8, and MapSubwindows have canonical regression coverage.
A matched server/tswm/terminal profile records CPU, PSS/private memory, faults, context switches, syscalls, startup, and compositor counters with limitations.

title: [performance] Compare matched tswm sessions on control :5 and frame :7
outcome: Run one reproducible directional comparison with tswm on an Xorg-compatible control display :5 and frame :7, excluding any viewer bridge.
audit: Inventory Xvfb/Xorg, frame --fbtest, x11perf, tswm and tswm-mcp binaries, display isolation, process attribution, and host noise controls.
acceptance: Both sessions use identical geometry, tswm profile, clients, workload, affinity, durations, and sample order.
x11perf uses only supported comparable operations and reports unsupported cases honestly.
Raw JSON separates server, tswm, clients, MCP, and total session with host/load caveats.

title: [protocol] Launch and render Firefox with an isolated local profile
outcome: Launch Firefox against frame with an isolated offline profile and render a deterministic local page without blocking the server.
audit: Capture setup/core/extension requests from the first launch, classify every unhandled reply-bearing request, and compare each required semantic with xorgproto/X.Org.
acceptance: Firefox maps a visible top-level window and deterministic local test page.
Startup has no reply-bearing deadlock, stream desynchronization, server crash, or unrelated-client failure.
Required XKB, XI2, RandR, RENDER, SHM, Damage, XFixes, and Composite behavior is tested or explicitly bounded.

title: [input] Prove tswm dogfood focus, move, resize, drag, keyboard, pointer, and close flows
outcome: Demonstrate that mapped terminal and Firefox windows are actually usable through complete tswm interaction flows, not merely visible.
audit: Define semantic pre/postconditions for focus, pointer click, title drag, edge resize, keyboard input, scrolling, maximize/restore, close, and interrupted-client cases.
acceptance: Each flow changes the intended window/geometry/state and leaves no stuck grab or cursor.
Terminal text input and Firefox local-page interaction work after repeated move/resize cycles.
The control display and frame use the same scripted flow, with MCP audit plus pixel fallback only where needed.

title: [agents] Drive frame compatibility sessions through tswm MCP with audit evidence
outcome: Use tswm's permissioned MCP graph, observation, and action surfaces to inspect and exercise frame sessions with an append-only audit trail.
audit: Inventory tswm-mcp initialize/tools/list/tools/call, read-only DesktopGraph, pixel policy, action allowlists, current move/resize gaps, and frame extension requirements.
acceptance: MCP reads identify expected windows, focus, workspace, geometry, class, and stacking on control and frame displays.
Mutations are allowlisted, dry-run capable, audited, and never bypass tswm's action registry.
Pixel capture is explicit fallback; benchmark attribution excludes observation/viewer costs unless separately reported.

title: [protocol] Validate the representative desktop client compatibility matrix
outcome: Define and pass a bounded client matrix covering terminal, browser, toolkit, graphics, and window-manager behavior required for v1.0.
audit: Select clients/versions by protocol coverage and user value, then capture startup/interaction traces and deterministic local fixtures.
acceptance: The matrix declares exact versions, scenarios, expected results, limitations, and evidence artifacts.
A launch-only result is not accepted without the interaction scenario assigned to that client.
Failures become scoped protocol/extension/input/render issues under the owning epic.

title: [performance] Compare standalone Xorg and frame on an idle bare console
outcome: Compare sequential standalone Xorg and frame sessions owning the same idle machine, GPU, VT, tswm profile, and workload without Xephyr/Xvfb/viewer overhead.
audit: Record the host Xorg driver stack, frame DRM path, display-manager state, recovery route, workload, affinity/governor, GPU/energy counters, and process attribution before running.
acceptance: No other graphical session owns DRM and a human controls the recoverable TTY run.
Alternating repeated samples report startup, CPU, memory, faults, syscalls, wakeups, scheduler wait, GPU, energy, and compositor counters.
The original display manager and console recover and raw artifacts include all caveats.
dependencies: needs-human-session: idle host and recoverable TTY
